faqs.q: How much does a backyard game court cost in Austin?
faqs.a: Austin Courts & Floors puts backyard game courts at about $25–$35 per square foot. Their published ranges run from $15,000–$42,000 for a shooting court to $40,000–$80,500 for a pickleball court and $120,000–$250,000 for a tennis court.

faqs.q: How much does a modular gym floor cost?
faqs.a: Typically $8–$12 per square foot for a new modular gym floor, not including subfloor prep, accessories or maintenance. A 5,000 sq ft gym runs roughly $40,000–$60,000.

faqs.q: How long has Austin Courts & Floors been building courts?
faqs.a: Since 1978. The company was formerly Sport Court of Austin and describes itself as the original and longest-operating court builder in Austin and Central Texas.

faqs.q: How much space does a pickleball, basketball or tennis court need?
faqs.a: Per NexCourt: a regulation pickleball court is 24' x 65' overall (20' x 44' playing area, 30' x 60' ideal for competitive play); a full NBA/NCAA basketball court is 94' x 50'; a full tennis court is 60' x 120' (36' x 78' playing area). Smaller variations are possible.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build a court?
faqs.a: It depends on site and design choices, but a concrete base must cure for 30 days before surfacing, fencing or lights go in, per NexCourt.

faqs.q: Can you build a court on a sloped yard?
faqs.a: Yes. NexCourt says excavation equipment can create a flat pad when needed.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with a NexCourt modular court?
faqs.a: NexCourt's limited warranty covers the tile surfacing for 16 years.

faqs.q: Do court builders in Texas need a license?
faqs.a: Texas does not license general contractors. NexCourt says it is bonded and insured, gets licensed where a city requires it, and uses only licensed electricians.

prices.label: Multi-purpose backyard court
prices.text: Typically $30,000–$75,000 depending on site prep, size, surface, lights and fencing

faqs.q: How much does a backyard basketball or multi-sport court cost in Georgia?
faqs.a: CBA Sports says multi-purpose courts typically range from $30,000 to $75,000, depending on site prep, size, surface, lighting and fencing.

faqs.q: How much space do I need for a backyard basketball court?
faqs.a: Per CBA Sports: a half court can be as small as 25' x 25'; a full three-point line needs at least 42' of width; their recommended minimum full court is about 36' x 66'.

faqs.q: Is concrete or asphalt better under a court?
faqs.a: CBA Sports recommends concrete as the most durable, longest-lasting base; cracks in asphalt are structural and can only be repaired cosmetically.

faqs.q: Which court surface is easiest on the joints?
faqs.a: Modular tiles and rubber hybrid systems add cushioning; standard acrylic coatings do not, per CBA Sports.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit or HOA approval for a backyard court?
faqs.a: It depends on your county and city zoning. HOAs usually ask for plans and drawings before approving, per CBA Sports.

faqs.q: What areas does Court Builders of St. Louis serve?

stats: Courts in Las Vegas still in play after 30+ years

faqs.q: How much does it cost to build a pickleball court in Las Vegas?
faqs.a: Legendary Sports Construction says a standard outdoor acrylic pickleball court typically runs $20,000–$35,000. They give itemized quotes after a site visit rather than per-foot prices.

faqs.q: Can a sport court hold up to desert heat?
faqs.a: Yes, if it's built for it: UV-stable acrylic coatings, a base engineered for soil movement, and planning for orientation and shade, per Legendary.

faqs.q: What court surfaces are available?
faqs.a: Legendary offers poured acrylic, cushioned acrylic, modular tile, turf and hardwood, chosen by sport and use.

faqs.q: Do Las Vegas court builders work with HOAs?
faqs.a: Legendary builds for HOAs, apartments, resorts, schools and parks, and prepares layouts, colors and renderings for design-review committees.
